key_insight: Small-radius, high-electronegativity A-site dopants like Ca can simultaneously improve proton transport and chemical stability in BaCeO3-based electrolytes by weakening A–O bonding and modifying lattice chemistry.
engineering_relevance: A-site doping provides a practical design lever for proton-conducting solid oxide fuel cell electrolytes that need both higher conductivity and better resistance to CO2/SO2 degradation.
method: Mechanistic analysis of A-site size/electronegativity effects
Assessment of proton transport, vacancy formation, and gas adsorption trends
evidence_signal: The abstract reports computed improvements in oxygen-vacancy formation, proton uptake, impurity-phase suppression, reduced CO2/SO2 adsorption, and potential grain-boundary resistance mitigation.
watch_item: Benefits may depend on whether proton transfer is the rate-limiting step and on controlling Ca segregation or other microstructural effects in real electrolytes.
paper_title: Role of small-radius and high-electronegativity A-Site dopants in enhancing proton transport and stability of perovskite electrolytes
